dispositions.reason: Current migrations, functions, tests, and canonical docs retain product-user records keyed by auth user ID and contain no product_customers table, join-trigger creation, backfill, or access-revocation preservation contract. The candidate is an explicitly proposed product policy, so current absence cannot settle it.

The repository documents product-user access, roles, and profile management, but has no implemented customer-management resource or explicit ghost-to-identity merge contract. The requested resource split and audit rules remain an open architectural decision rather than a verified durable contract.

Product scoping is implemented for existing ClassKit resources, but no customer identity, contact-match, cross-product discovery, or merge flow exists in the checked repository to establish this proposed privacy policy. It must be explicitly decided before canonical documentation can state it.

Current implementation uses class_kit.users and user_id-backed memberships, registrations, and attendance; no product_customers or nullable auth_user_id contract was found. The candidate requests a new durable identity model and retains an explicit profile-ownership uncertainty, so it is not promoted from proposal wording.

Current code and regression tests support the existing product-user/auth boundary, not customer_id-backed memberships, registrations, attendance, or progress. This is a proposed replacement architecture and requires an explicit accepted decision before it can change Project Memory.

Verification found no customer API resource, ghost-link operation, or approved contract separating it from application-access management. The handoff asks for a policy decision, which current incidental product-user implementation cannot supply.

The current repository enforces product scoping for its existing resources, but has no customer identity/linking flow to verify the proposed per-product customer uniqueness or cross-product match behavior. This remains downstream product and engineering work.

No implementation evidence establishes product_customers, nullable auth_user_id, or customer_id-backed operational records. The handoff describes a possible future boundary, not current durable behavior.

The card-oriented ghost-customer and merge follow-up is an unimplemented product/engineering decision. It cannot be represented as current Project Memory without an approved design and repository evidence.

Current class handler code and its focused regression test establish the observable direct-get result: an ineligible members-only class returns generic 403 forbidden, while a missing otherwise-visible class returns 404. The corrected discovery and membership-eligibility prose records this contract. repository-identity.json was also inspected as run evidence and conflicts with the authored no-remote claim in target-repo/docs/repositories/structure.md; it did not drive canonical prose.

The final draft now documents the direct-get 403 result, list omission, template-bound eligibility, and registration precedence using current handler, migration, and regression-test evidence. This overlapping handoff therefore needs no separate documentation change.
